topic: Writing Paragraph (Question No. 12: ঋতুপূর্ণ সমসাময়িক বিষয় ও জাতীয় ঘটনা নিয়ে প্যারাগ্রাফ)

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Reading Books” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Books open doors to knowledge, imagination and understanding. A reader can learn about distant places, meet characters from different backgrounds and explore ideas that may not appear in a classroom lesson. Reading is therefore both useful and enjoyable. Different books serve different purposes. Textbooks explain school subjects, while stories help us imagine how other people feel. Biographies introduce the lives and efforts of individuals, and science books encourage us to ask questions about the world. A newspaper or a reference book can also help us find information, although we should check important claims against reliable sources. I try to read for a short period each day. When a word is unfamiliar, I note it down and look up its meaning. Later I discuss an interesting passage with a friend. Reading does not mean accepting every idea without thought; it means considering ideas carefully and asking questions. In this way books become companions as well as teachers. A steady reading habit can enrich our lives for many years.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “Tree Plantation” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Trees are essential to a healthy environment. They provide shade, shelter for wildlife and useful products such as fruit and timber. Their roots help hold soil in place, while their leaves contribute to the natural processes that support life. Planting and protecting trees is therefore an important responsibility. In many places trees are cut down to make room for roads, buildings or farms. Some development is necessary, but careless removal can leave land exposed to erosion and reduce habitats for birds and other animals. In hot weather, a tree-lined playground or street can also offer welcome shade. Planting suitable trees can help restore some of these benefits. Schools can organise supervised planting days and prepare a watering schedule. Communities can also protect existing trees and replace those lost to storms or disease. Everyone can take part by caring for a plant or learning why local species matter. If we combine careful planting with long-term care, the trees we nurture today can benefit future generations.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Journey by Train” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A journey by train can be both comfortable and memorable. Last winter I travelled with my family to visit relatives in another town. It was my first long train journey, and I was excited from the moment we reached the station. The platform was busy with passengers carrying bags and looking for their coaches. We checked our tickets and waited safely behind the platform edge. When the train arrived, we found our seats and placed our luggage where it would not block the aisle. Soon the train began to move, and the station slowly disappeared from view. The journey took several hours, but I did not feel bored. When we reached our destination, our relatives were waiting to welcome us. The trip taught me that a journey is not merely a way to reach a place; it can also be a chance to observe people, enjoy nature and spend time with family.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Duties of a Student” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Student life is a time for learning, building good habits and discovering interests. A student's main duty is to study sincerely, but education includes much more than memorising lessons for examinations. It also involves responsibility towards family, school and the wider community. A responsible student attends classes regularly, listens carefully and asks questions when a lesson is unclear. Preparing a realistic timetable helps balance schoolwork, rest and recreation. Students should complete their own work honestly instead of using unfair means. A mistake is an opportunity to learn, and teachers can help when a topic is difficult. Students also need exercise, adequate sleep and time for creative activities. Joining a club or taking part in a supervised community project can develop cooperation and confidence. Above all, learning should help us become thoughtful and kind citizens. By doing our duties regularly, we prepare ourselves not only for examinations but also for the responsibilities of adult life.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “Physical Exercise” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Physical exercise is an important part of a healthy life. It keeps the body active and can help us feel refreshed. Walking, cycling, swimming and playing games are examples of exercise, and different people may enjoy different activities. Regular movement helps develop strength and fitness. Team games can also teach cooperation, patience and respect for rules. Exercise gives students a break from long hours of sitting and studying. It can be more enjoyable when friends or family members participate together. However, exercise alone is not enough: healthy food, safe drinking water and sufficient sleep are important too. I enjoy walking and playing badminton with my friends. These activities make me feel energetic and help me return to my studies with a clear mind. The best routine is one that is safe and enjoyable enough to follow regularly. By making room for movement in our daily lives, we can support our physical and mental well-being.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Book Fair” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A book fair brings readers, writers and publishers together. It offers a pleasant opportunity to discover books, share ideas and celebrate the habit of reading. I visited a book fair with my classmates and a teacher last year, and the experience remains fresh in my mind. The fair was held in a large open area with rows of colourful stalls. Publishers displayed storybooks, poems, children's magazines and books on science and history. Visitors moved from stall to stall, examining covers and discussing their favourite authors. Some stalls had small spaces where writers spoke to readers about their work. A book fair is more than a place to buy things. It encourages people to explore new ideas and helps young readers develop curiosity. Those who cannot buy many books can still discover titles to look for in a library. We returned home tired but happy, carrying books and many ideas to discuss. I hope to visit another fair soon.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Clean Water” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Clean water is essential for life. People need safe water for drinking, cooking and personal hygiene, and farmers need it to grow crops. Animals and plants also depend on water, so protecting water sources benefits the whole environment. Water can become polluted when rubbish, sewage or harmful chemicals enter rivers, ponds and other sources. Drinking contaminated water can cause illness. For this reason families should use a safe supply and follow local health guidance on treating water when necessary. Storing drinking water in clean, covered containers also helps protect it from contamination. During a flood or other emergency, a normally safe source may become contaminated. In such circumstances we should listen to reliable local advice rather than assume the water is safe. Clean water should be available to everyone, not treated as a luxury. By using it carefully and working together to protect it, we support health, farming and the natural world.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A School Garden” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A school garden is a place where students can learn about plants while making their surroundings attractive. Our school has a small garden beside the playground. Teachers and students work together to care for it, and it has become one of my favourite places. At the beginning of the term we prepared the soil with the help of a gardener. We planted flower seeds and a few vegetables in separate beds. Each group received a simple task, such as watering, removing weeds or keeping a record of growth. Our science teacher explained why plants need suitable light, water and soil. A garden needs regular care, including during holidays. For this reason we make a schedule and ask school staff to supervise the work. I enjoy watching a seedling grow over several weeks. Our garden reminds us that a small effort, repeated patiently, can create something beautiful and useful.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Value of Time” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Time is one of the most valuable resources in life. Once a moment has passed, we cannot bring it back. Learning to use time wisely helps students complete their duties while still leaving room for rest, friendship and enjoyment. A timetable is a useful guide, but it should be realistic. We can set aside time for school lessons, homework, exercise and sleep. Difficult tasks may be divided into smaller steps so that they do not feel overwhelming. Starting revision early can reduce pressure before an examination. When plans change, we can adjust them instead of giving up altogether. Punctuality also shows respect for other people's time. Arriving on time for school and keeping promises help build trust. At the same time, we should be understanding when someone faces circumstances beyond their control. By planning carefully and choosing our priorities, we can make each day more balanced and meaningful.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Rainy Day” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A rainy day brings a special change to the familiar landscape. Dark clouds gather, the air becomes cooler and the sound of falling rain fills the surroundings. Some people enjoy the change, while others face difficulties travelling or working outdoors. One morning last monsoon, rain began just as I was preparing for school. I carried an umbrella and walked carefully along the wet road with my neighbour. Trees looked freshly washed, and small drops hung from their leaves. At school many students arrived with wet shoes, but our teachers made sure we entered the classrooms safely. After school I stayed indoors, read a story and listened to the rain on the roof. In the evening the clouds cleared and the garden looked bright again. That day reminded me of both the beauty and the responsibilities that come with the rainy season. Keeping drains clear and following local safety advice can help our communities cope better when rain is heavy.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Village Market” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A village market is an important meeting place for people in the countryside. It is usually held once or twice a week in an open space. Farmers, shopkeepers and customers come from neighbouring villages. At the market, vegetables, fish, fruit and household goods are arranged in separate areas. Some sellers sit under temporary roofs, while others spread their goods on mats. Buyers compare prices and choose what they need. The calls of vendors and the conversations of customers make the place lively. The market helps farmers sell their produce without travelling to a distant town. It also gives small traders an opportunity to earn a living. However, waste and muddy paths can cause inconvenience. Proper bins, clean water and regular cleaning would make the market safer and more pleasant. A well-managed village market serves both the local economy and the community.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A School Library” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A school library is a quiet place where students can read and borrow books. It is an important part of a school because learning should not be limited to textbooks. A good library encourages curiosity and independent study. Our library has shelves of stories, biographies, dictionaries and books on science and history. Students can consult reference books when preparing a project. The librarian helps us find suitable books and keeps a record of those we borrow. There are tables where we can sit and read during free periods. We must follow some simple rules. We should speak softly, handle books carefully and return them on time. Writing on pages or tearing them prevents others from enjoying the same books. A reading club can make the library even more welcoming by allowing students to share their favourite stories. A useful library helps build thoughtful readers and makes school life richer.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “My Favourite Hobby” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
My favourite hobby is gardening. It gives me pleasure and teaches me to be patient. I do not need a large field; a few pots on a balcony or a small patch of soil can be enough to begin. I grow flowers and some vegetables with help from my family. First, I loosen the soil and choose healthy seeds or seedlings. I water the plants when they need it and remove weeds carefully. Sometimes insects damage the leaves, so I ask an experienced gardener for safe advice rather than using chemicals carelessly. The most exciting moment comes when a seedling produces its first flower or fruit. Not every plant survives, but a failure helps me learn about sunlight, water and soil. Gardening also makes our surroundings greener. It gives me a useful break from study and reminds me that living things need steady care. I hope to continue this hobby as I grow older.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Journey by Boat” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Last autumn I went on a boat journey with my family. We visited relatives who live across a river. The sky was clear, and the water shone in the morning sunlight. Before boarding, we checked that the boat was not overcrowded and followed the boatman's instructions. I sat beside my mother and watched the banks move slowly past us. Fishermen were working in small boats, and children waved from near their homes. Green fields and patches of trees stretched beyond the water. The boatman told us how the river changes with the seasons. We carried our own drinking water and kept our bags away from the edge. After a peaceful journey, we reached the other bank, where our relatives welcomed us. I enjoyed the scenery and learned that a river is both a beautiful part of nature and an important route for local people. The memory of the trip still makes me happy.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Winter Morning” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A winter morning has a special beauty in Bangladesh. The air is cool, and fog often covers fields, roads and trees. People may wake to find drops of dew on grass and spiderwebs. In villages, farmers begin their work despite the cold. Some people gather around a small fire to warm themselves. As the sun rises, the fog slowly disappears and the surroundings become clearer. Families may enjoy warm pitha and date juice where these are available and safely prepared. Winter is pleasant for many people, but it can be difficult for those who lack warm clothes or shelter. We can share clean blankets and clothing through trustworthy local groups. We should also take care around fires and help younger children stay warm. A winter morning is memorable not only for its natural beauty but also for the kindness it can inspire among neighbours.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “My Aim in Life” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Everyone needs a goal to give direction to hard work. My aim is to become a doctor and serve people who have difficulty getting medical care. This ambition grew when I saw how a kind doctor patiently explained treatment to a worried family. A doctor must have knowledge, practical skills and compassion. To prepare, I need to study science carefully, develop good habits and learn to communicate clearly. I should also listen to teachers and ask questions when I do not understand a lesson. Becoming a doctor takes many years of education and supervised training, so I must be ready to work steadily. I hope one day to serve in a community where medical services are limited. I would treat patients with respect and encourage them to seek reliable health advice. My goal may be difficult, but it motivates me to use my time well. Whatever profession I finally choose, I want my work to benefit others.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A School Sports Day” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Our annual school sports day is one of the happiest events of the year. It brings students, teachers and families together and gives everyone a chance to enjoy games and friendly competition. Before the event, teachers prepare the field and explain the rules. Students practise races and other activities suitable for their age. On the day itself, the programme begins with a welcome speech. Some students take part in running events, while others cheer for their classmates. Teachers supervise the activities and make sure that drinking water and first aid are available. Winning a prize is exciting, but participation matters too. Players learn to respect rules, accept results and congratulate one another. At the end, prizes are distributed and everyone thanks the organisers. The event shows that sport is not only about winning; it also builds confidence, cooperation and friendship. I look forward to it every year.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Learning English” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
English is an international language used in education, business and communication. Learning it can help us read books, understand useful information and communicate with people from different countries. It also gives students access to many learning resources. Learning English does not mean neglecting Bangla or any other language. Our mother tongue is central to our identity, and knowing more than one language is an advantage. To improve English, we should practise reading, writing, listening and speaking regularly. Simple stories, conversations and class activities can make practice enjoyable. Mistakes are a natural part of learning. Instead of being afraid, students should ask for help and try again. Keeping a vocabulary notebook and using new words in sentences can be useful. With patience and regular practice, we can become more confident. English is a practical skill that can open opportunities while allowing us to share our own culture with others.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Visit to a Historical Place” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Last year I visited the historic city of Bagerhat with my family. I had read about its old buildings and was eager to see one of them. We visited the Sixty Dome Mosque, a famous example of Bengal's architectural heritage. The building impressed me with its thick walls, rows of pillars and many domes. A guide explained that it was associated with Khan Jahan Ali and the medieval settlement of Khalifatabad. I listened carefully and tried to imagine the people who had lived and worked in the area centuries ago. Visitors should respect a historical site. We avoided writing on the walls, put our rubbish in a bin and followed the rules at the entrance. The visit made history feel more real than a list of dates in a textbook. Such places help us understand earlier communities and their skills. Protecting them allows future generations to learn from them too.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “My Favourite Game” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
My favourite game is football. It is played by two teams, each trying to score by sending the ball into the opponent's goal. I like it because it is energetic and requires cooperation. I usually play with friends in a nearby field after school. Before starting, we agree on the boundaries and make sure the ground is reasonably safe. We pass the ball, defend together and encourage players who are still learning. When a disagreement occurs, we try to settle it calmly instead of arguing. Football helps me exercise and teaches me to think quickly. More importantly, it reminds me that a team succeeds when its members support one another. A good player respects opponents and accepts the referee's decision. We take breaks and drink water, especially in hot weather. Whether our team wins or loses, I enjoy the time spent with my friends and the lessons learned on the field.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Honesty” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Honesty means speaking the truth and acting without deception. It is an important quality because trust grows when people know that they can depend on one another. An honest person admits mistakes instead of hiding them. Students can practise honesty in many ordinary situations. They should complete their own work, avoid cheating and return something they find to its owner or a responsible adult. If they damage a friend's property, they should explain what happened and try to put it right. Telling the truth may sometimes be uncomfortable, but a lie can create greater problems later. Honesty should be combined with kindness. We can express a difficult truth politely and avoid hurting someone unnecessarily. Families, teachers and leaders can set examples by keeping promises and accepting responsibility. No one is perfect, but we can all make honest choices. Such choices build strong friendships and a more trustworthy society.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Life of a Farmer” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A farmer plays an essential role in society by producing food and other crops. In Bangladesh, many farmers work in fields, orchards or vegetable gardens. Their work requires knowledge, effort and careful attention to the seasons. A farmer prepares the soil, selects seeds and plants at a suitable time. Crops need water and protection from weeds and pests. Weather, floods, droughts and changes in prices can make farming uncertain. At harvest time, the farmer gathers the crop and arranges for it to be sold or stored. Farmers can benefit from reliable information, fair access to markets and suitable tools. Responsible use of water and soil helps protect the land for the future. Consumers should respect their work and avoid wasting food. Whenever I eat a meal, I try to remember the many people who helped produce it. A farmer's contribution deserves recognition and support.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Day at a Village Fair” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A village fair is a colourful event that brings people together. I visited one with my family during a local festival. We arrived in the afternoon and found the open ground full of stalls and visitors. Some stalls sold clay pots, toys, baskets and handmade ornaments. Others offered traditional snacks. I watched a craftsperson shape a small object and admired the patience required. Children enjoyed simple games while adults met friends and neighbours. We stayed together in the crowd and agreed on a meeting place in case anyone became separated. My favourite purchase was a small clay bird. We also listened to local music before returning home. A fair gives artisans and traders an opportunity to sell their goods, and it keeps local traditions alive. At the same time, organisers should provide clean facilities and manage crowds safely. The visit was enjoyable because it combined entertainment, craftsmanship and community spirit.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Punctuality” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Punctuality means doing things at the right time. A punctual person respects both personal responsibilities and other people's time. It is a habit that can be developed through planning and practice. A student who reaches school on time can attend the whole lesson and settle down before class begins. Preparing books and clothes the night before may prevent a rushed morning. A simple timetable can also help us complete homework without leaving everything until the last moment. However, unexpected illness, transport problems or family difficulties can delay anyone, so we should respond to others with understanding. Punctuality is valuable in workplaces and public services too. When a meeting or journey begins on time, everyone can plan more effectively. We should allow extra time for possible delays and inform others if we cannot arrive as promised. Being punctual does not mean being hurried all the time; it means managing our duties thoughtfully.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Village Doctor” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A village doctor is often a familiar figure in a rural community. People may turn to a local health worker when they are ill or need advice. Access to safe, qualified medical care is especially important where hospitals are far away. A trained doctor listens to a patient's symptoms, examines the patient when necessary and recommends appropriate care. Some problems require tests or treatment at a hospital. A responsible practitioner recognises these limits and refers patients to a qualified facility when needed. Patients should not take antibiotics or other medicines without proper medical advice. Health workers can also encourage vaccination, hygiene and safe drinking water. Their work becomes easier when communities have good roads, clinics and reliable supplies. We should appreciate compassionate service while checking a practitioner's qualifications. A healthy village needs both caring professionals and a health system that people can reach and trust.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Rainy Season in Bangladesh” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
The rainy season brings a major change to life in Bangladesh. Dark clouds gather, and frequent rain fills ponds, rivers and fields. The countryside becomes green, and many farmers welcome the water needed for crops. Rain also provides relief from the summer heat. Children enjoy watching raindrops fall, while boats become useful in some waterlogged areas. However, heavy rain can create serious problems. Roads may become muddy or flooded, classes may be interrupted, and low-lying homes can be damaged. Floods can also make safe drinking water harder to obtain. Communities can prepare by keeping drains clear, listening to official warnings and helping vulnerable neighbours reach safe places. We should avoid floodwater where possible because it may hide dangers or contamination. The rainy season is therefore a time of beauty as well as caution. Careful preparation helps people enjoy its benefits and face its difficulties.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Street Hawker” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A street hawker sells goods by moving from place to place or standing near a busy street. A hawker may carry fruit, toys, household items or other small products. This work is familiar in many towns and villages. The hawker often begins early and spends long hours attracting customers. Buyers appreciate being able to purchase useful goods near their homes. For the seller, each sale contributes to daily income. The work can be difficult in rain, heat or heavy traffic, and earnings may vary from day to day. Hawkers deserve respect and safe working conditions. At the same time, selling areas should be arranged so that pedestrians, including people with disabilities, can move safely. Food sellers need access to clean water and hygienic facilities. A practical arrangement should consider the needs of both sellers and the public. The street hawker's work shows the importance of small businesses in everyday life.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “My Favourite Teacher” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A good teacher can inspire students to learn and become better people. My favourite teacher is our English teacher, who combines clear explanations with patience and kindness. In class, she begins a lesson with a question and invites us to share our ideas. She reads stories aloud and helps us notice new words in context. When we make mistakes, she explains how to improve instead of making us feel ashamed. She also encourages quiet students to participate, while allowing them time to think. What I admire most is her fairness. She listens to different opinions and treats students with respect. She reminds us to be honest in our work and helpful to our classmates. Her lessons have made me more confident about speaking English. I know that learning requires my own effort, but her guidance makes that effort enjoyable. I hope to follow her example of patience and responsibility.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Benefits of Morning Walks” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A morning walk can be a refreshing way to begin the day. The air may feel cooler, and familiar streets or fields look different in the early light. Walking regularly can also be part of a healthy routine. I sometimes walk with a family member along a safe path near our home. We choose a comfortable pace and wear suitable shoes. During the walk we notice birds, trees and people beginning their daily work. After returning, I feel ready to wash, eat breakfast and prepare for school. A walk should be adapted to a person's health and circumstances. A busy road, poor lighting or unsafe weather may make another time or place a better choice. People with health concerns can seek advice from a qualified professional. Walking alone cannot replace good food and adequate sleep, but it is a simple activity that many people can enjoy. A regular walk can benefit both body and mind.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Visit to a Zoo” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
During a school holiday, I visited a zoo with my family. I was excited to see animals I had previously known only from books and pictures. At the entrance, we read the visitor rules and planned our route. We saw several kinds of birds, deer and other animals. A keeper explained why animals need suitable food, shelter and space. I enjoyed watching their different movements, but I also realised that wild animals have complex needs that cannot always be met easily in captivity. We did not feed the animals or throw objects into their enclosures. Instead, we observed quietly and kept the grounds clean. A responsible zoo should protect animal welfare and help visitors learn about conservation. Protecting natural habitats is equally important because animals belong to wider ecosystems. The visit was enjoyable, but it also taught me to think carefully about our responsibilities towards other living creatures.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Good Manners” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Good manners are ways of showing respect and consideration for others. Saying please and thank you, listening without interrupting and speaking politely can make everyday interactions more pleasant. Manners begin at home but are useful everywhere. At school, students can greet teachers, wait their turn and help keep shared spaces clean. On public transport, offering a seat to someone who needs it is a thoughtful act. Online, good manners include avoiding hurtful messages and respecting other people's privacy. Politeness does not mean agreeing with everything. We can express disagreement honestly without insulting another person. We should also remember that customs differ and that a person's disability or circumstances may affect how they communicate. The purpose of manners is not to judge people by rigid rules, but to make others feel respected. Small acts of courtesy can build trust and make a community more welcoming.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “My First Day at School” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
I still remember my first day at a new school. I felt excited, but I was also nervous because I did not know the teachers or the other students. My parent accompanied me to the gate and encouraged me to be brave. A teacher welcomed the new students and showed us our classroom. I chose a seat beside a child who smiled and introduced herself. During the first lesson, we learned the names of our teachers and talked about the subjects we would study. At break time, my new friend showed me where to find drinking water and the library. By the end of the day, my fear had become curiosity. I understood that many other students were nervous too. The kindness of my teacher and classmate helped me feel that I belonged. That day taught me how important a warm welcome can be for someone entering an unfamiliar place.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Education” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Education helps people develop knowledge, skills and judgment. It allows us to understand the world, communicate with others and make informed choices. Learning takes place at school, at home and throughout life. At school, students study language, mathematics, science and many other subjects. They also learn to cooperate, solve problems and ask questions. A good education should encourage curiosity rather than mere memorisation. Teachers, families and communities all have a role in supporting learners. Education alone cannot solve every social problem, but it gives people tools to participate and improve their lives. When everyone has a fair chance to learn, the whole community benefits from their ideas and abilities.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Flood in Our Area” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A flood can change ordinary life very quickly. In this imagined account, heavy rain caused the river near our area to rise above its banks. Water entered roads and some homes, and many families had to leave for safer places. My family listened to local announcements and packed important documents, drinking water and essential medicines. We moved to a designated shelter with our neighbours. Volunteers helped elderly people and children, while local workers shared information about food and safe water. We stayed away from electrical wires and did not walk through fast-moving water. After the water went down, families returned to assess the damage. Cleaning homes and repairing belongings took time. The experience showed how important early warnings, safe shelters and community cooperation are. Floods can cause great suffering, but preparation and mutual help can reduce risks. We should support recovery and learn from each event.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Picnic I Enjoyed” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Last winter our class went on a picnic with our teachers. We travelled to a park outside town and spent a pleasant day playing, eating and exploring together. Everyone was excited when we gathered at school in the morning. Before leaving, the teachers counted the students and explained the safety rules. At the park, we spread mats in a shaded area and shared the food we had brought. Later we played games, sang songs and walked along a marked path. A teacher helped organise a friendly quiz, and even those who did not win enjoyed taking part. Before going home, we collected our rubbish and checked that no belongings were left behind. The return journey was quieter because everyone was tired. The picnic gave us a welcome break from our usual routine and helped us know our classmates better. Its happiest lesson was that a simple day becomes special when people cooperate and care for one another.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Saving Water” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Water is necessary for drinking, cooking, farming and cleanliness. Although rain and rivers are familiar in Bangladesh, safe water is not always available where and when people need it. Saving water and protecting its sources are therefore important. At home, we can turn off a tap while brushing our teeth and repair leaks promptly. We can use only the water needed for washing and reuse suitable water for plants when it is safe to do so. Farmers and communities can also plan irrigation carefully to reduce waste. Saving water is not enough if sources become polluted. Rubbish, sewage and harmful chemicals should not be allowed to enter ponds and rivers. Local authorities and communities share responsibility for safe water systems. Children can help by reporting a leaking tap and keeping their surroundings clean. Small daily actions, combined with effective public services, can protect this essential resource for the future.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Memorable Birthday” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
My last birthday was memorable not because of expensive gifts, but because of the time I spent with my family and friends. We decided to celebrate simply at home after school. My younger sister helped decorate the room with paper shapes. My parents prepared a favourite meal, and a few friends came in the afternoon. We played a guessing game and shared a cake. One friend gave me a handmade card containing a poem, which made me smile. We also took some food to a neighbour who could not join us. At the end of the celebration, everyone helped clear the table and put away the decorations. I felt grateful for the effort people had made to be together. The day reminded me that happiness does not depend on spending a great deal of money. Thoughtful words, shared laughter and kindness can make an ordinary room feel very special.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Road Safety” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Road safety is a shared responsibility. Pedestrians, drivers, passengers and authorities all have roles in reducing accidents. Careful behaviour and safe road design can protect lives. Pedestrians should use footpaths and marked crossings where available. Before crossing, they should look carefully in both directions and avoid being distracted by a phone. Children may need help from an adult on busy roads. Passengers should wait in a safe place and avoid boarding a moving vehicle. No single action can prevent every accident, and people do not always have access to safe infrastructure. Nevertheless, attention, planning and cooperation can make journeys safer for everyone. We should treat road safety as a daily duty rather than an occasional concern.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A School Magazine” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork produced by students and teachers. It may include poems, stories, essays, drawings and reports about school activities. The magazine gives young writers a chance to share their ideas. To prepare an issue, an editorial team invites contributions and selects suitable work. Teachers can help students correct language and check facts without removing their individual voices. Contributors should submit their own work or acknowledge any material they use with permission. The team then organises the pages and checks the final copy before publication. A magazine encourages creativity, cooperation and careful reading. A student who is shy in class may find confidence through a poem or illustration. A printed or digital edition can also preserve memories of the school year. If everyone has a fair opportunity to contribute, the magazine becomes a lively record of the whole school community.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Uses and Abuses of the Internet” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
The internet connects people to information and services across the world. Students can use it to attend lessons, consult reference materials and communicate with teachers. It also helps people find news, conduct business and stay in touch with relatives. However, not everything online is reliable. False information can spread quickly, so important claims should be checked against trustworthy sources. Spending too much time on games or social media can also interfere with sleep and study. Online strangers may try to trick people into sharing personal information. We should use strong passwords, keep them private and ask a trusted adult for help when something seems suspicious. It is wise to think before posting and to treat others respectfully. A balanced schedule leaves time for study, exercise and family. The internet is a useful tool when we use it carefully, critically and with respect for our own safety and that of others.
items.page: Adapted from the existing original English 2nd Paper composition draft; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Tea Stall” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A tea stall is a familiar meeting place in many parts of Bangladesh. It may stand beside a market, a road or a bus stop. A small stall often has a counter, a kettle and a few benches. The owner boils water, prepares tea and serves customers in cups. Some stalls also sell biscuits, bread or snacks. Customers may include workers, travellers, shopkeepers and students. People often sit there to talk about the weather, sports or local news. A tea stall can offer a brief rest during a busy day. The owner works hard from morning until evening and depends on customers for a living. Clean water, covered food and washed cups are important for health. Waste should be placed in a bin, and hot kettles should be handled carefully. Though simple, a clean and friendly tea stall can be a useful part of neighbourhood life.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A School Canteen” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A school canteen provides students and teachers with food and drinks during breaks. It should be a clean, welcoming place where everyone can buy an affordable snack. A good canteen offers fresh food and safe drinking water. Its workers wash their hands, keep utensils clean and cover food properly. Students should stand in a queue and wait for their turn. They should avoid wasting food and put wrappers in the proper bin. A canteen can also encourage healthy choices by offering fruit and other nourishing snacks. The school authorities need to check prices and cleanliness regularly. Canteen workers deserve respect because they serve many people in a short time. If students follow the rules and the staff maintain hygiene, the canteen can make the school day more comfortable. It is not merely a shop; it is also a place to practise courtesy and responsibility.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Public Park” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A public park is an open place where people can enjoy fresh air and spend time outdoors. It may contain trees, paths, benches and a playground. Children can play while adults walk, exercise or sit quietly. Trees provide shade and make the surroundings pleasant for visitors. Birds and insects may also find shelter among the plants. A well-maintained park needs safe paths, clean toilets and waste bins. Visitors should avoid damaging plants or leaving rubbish behind. Children should use play equipment carefully and follow any safety rules. Community members and local authorities can work together to maintain the grounds. A park is especially valuable in a crowded town where many families have little open space at home. It offers a place to meet neighbours, rest and appreciate nature. With care from everyone, a public park can remain pleasant for many years.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A School Debate” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A school debate is an organised discussion in which students present different views on a topic. It teaches them to think carefully, listen and speak with confidence. Before the event, each team studies the subject and selects useful reasons and examples. Speakers practise presenting their points within the allotted time. During the debate, participants should pay attention to the other side and respond politely. A strong argument depends on clear evidence rather than personal attacks. A chairperson helps maintain order, and judges may evaluate the teams according to agreed rules. Students in the audience can also learn by considering both sides. After the result, everyone should respect the decision and congratulate the participants. A debate does not mean that friends must agree on every issue. Instead, it shows that disagreement can be handled fairly. Regular practice can improve research, communication and respect for different opinions.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Village Post Office” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A village post office connects people with services and communication beyond their neighbourhood. It may occupy a modest building near a market or a road. People visit it to send letters, receive parcels and use the services available at that branch. Postal workers sort items, record transactions and guide visitors. Some residents may also use financial services where these are offered. A letter can carry news, greetings or important documents to someone far away. Even when mobile phones make instant communication possible, physical parcels and documents still need reliable delivery. Customers should write clear addresses and keep any receipts they receive. The staff work carefully to protect the items entrusted to them. A clean waiting area and clear information make the office easier to use. A well-run post office can save villagers a long journey and help them stay connected with others.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Science Fair” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A science fair gives students an opportunity to show ideas and experiments to others. Groups choose topics, prepare models and explain what they have learned. A display might show a simple water filter, a weather chart or the life cycle of a plant. Students should test their work before the fair and describe its limitations honestly. Teachers supervise activities and make sure that materials are safe. Visitors can ask questions, and the young presenters practise answering clearly. A good project does not have to be expensive; careful observation and a clear explanation matter more. Students also learn to share tasks and solve problems together. Judges may recognise creativity, accuracy and presentation. Even a project that does not work as expected can teach an important lesson. A science fair makes learning active and encourages curiosity. It can inspire students to ask better questions about the world around them.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A School Assembly” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A school assembly brings students and teachers together at the beginning of the day or on a special occasion. It may include announcements, a song, a reading or a short talk. Students gather in an orderly way and listen to the people speaking. Teachers can use the assembly to share important information and recognise good work. A student may present a poem or speak about a useful habit. The programme should be planned so that it is clear and suitable for everyone. Students who speak in public gain confidence through preparation and practice. Others learn to listen respectfully and follow instructions. During hot or rainy weather, the school should choose a safe arrangement for the gathering. An assembly can remind the whole school that it is a community. When everyone participates with courtesy, it provides an organised and positive start to the day.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “The Importance of Handwashing” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
Handwashing is a simple habit that helps reduce the spread of many germs. We touch door handles, desks, money and other objects throughout the day. Germs can pass from our hands to food or to our eyes, nose and mouth. Washing with soap and clean running water is especially important before eating and after using the toilet. We should rub all parts of our hands, including between the fingers and around the nails, and then rinse and dry them. Schools can help by providing soap and water where possible. Families can encourage young children to practise the habit regularly. Handwashing does not replace every other health measure, but it is an important part of daily hygiene. Keeping shared surfaces clean and covering coughs also help protect others. A small action repeated at the right times can make homes and schools healthier for everyone.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A Power Cut” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A power cut is an interruption in the supply of electricity. It can affect homes, shops, schools and offices. Lights and fans stop working, and people may be unable to use electric devices. In hot weather the loss of a fan can make a room uncomfortable. Students may need another safe source of light to finish their homework. Families should handle candles carefully and keep them away from children and flammable materials. If a torch is available, it can be a safer way to move around in the dark. Shops may need to protect food that requires refrigeration. During a long interruption, people should follow advice from the electricity provider and local authorities. Saving energy and maintaining electrical equipment are useful habits, though they do not prevent every outage. A power cut reminds us how much daily life depends on a reliable supply of electricity.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.

items.text: 12. Write a paragraph on “A School Excursion” in about 150 words.
items.explanation:
Sample paragraph:
A school excursion is a planned educational visit outside the classroom. Students may visit a museum, a historical place or a nature centre with their teachers. Before travelling, the school informs families about the destination, schedule and safety rules. Students should arrive on time and stay with their assigned group. At the destination, they can observe objects and places that they have previously read about. Taking notes and asking respectful questions make the visit more meaningful. Teachers help students understand what they see and ensure that everyone is accounted for. Students should also avoid littering and follow the rules of the place. On the way back, they can discuss their favourite discoveries. Later, a short report or drawing can help them remember the experience. A well-organised excursion combines enjoyment with learning and gives students a chance to appreciate the world beyond school.
items.page: Original practice; model test Q12 format.
